title: Gemma 4 on a Tesla T4, Part 3: Int4 Embeddings Serve E2B in 2.86 GiB at 2.30x bf16
why_read: A rigorous, quantified benchmark on quantizing LLM embedding tables to 4-bit shows a concrete and substantial memory and throughput improvement with verified output correctness.
analysis: This article tackles the specific detail that in a quantized Gemma 4 E2B model, the embedding tables stay in 16-bit precision even though weights are already compressed, and on a memory-constrained Tesla T4 those embeddings end up dominating memory use. The author packs the embeddings down to 4-bit as well, cutting model load size from 6.33 to 2.86 GiB and roughly doubling usable KV cache capacity for handling more context. Critically, they verify that all greedy-decoded test outputs are token-identical to the higher precision version, which supports the claim that this optimization doesn't harm answer quality. The reported 11-37% throughput gain over Google's own official quantized export, backed by concrete numbers, makes this a genuinely useful technical result for anyone deploying small LLMs on budget GPUs.
